Harborlight Tool Library aims to streamline the management of tools, ensuring safety, accessibility, and efficiency. The library will implement a robust system to handle tool intake, testing, and maintenance. The intake process will use the amber intake label to identify tools, ensuring quick access for users. Safety is paramount, with every high-risk tool requiring two people for testing to prevent accidents. A weekly safety review on Wednesdays will ensure ongoing compliance with safety protocols. The access workflow for Harborlight Tool Library will be streamlined to enhance user convenience and safety. Users will be required to present a valid ID at the library entrance to access the tools. Upon entry, they will be directed to the intake counter where the amber intake label will be applied to each tool.

Tools will be categorized based on their risk level, with high-risk tools requiring additional testing procedures. Users will be provided with a tool card that includes the tool's name, description, and safety instructions. The card will also indicate the number of users allowed to borrow the tool at any given time to prevent overuse. To ensure a smooth transition of tools between volunteers, a volunteer handover system will be implemented. Each volunteer will be issued a tool logbook that records the tools they have borrowed and returned. The logbook will be checked by a supervisor before the volunteer leaves the library. This system will help in tracking the status of tools and ensure that no tools are left unattended or misused. Additionally, a weekly safety review will be conducted by the supervisor to discuss any issues or concerns with the tools and ensure that all safety protocols are followed.

Regular maintenance of tools is crucial to ensure their longevity and safety. Harborlight Tool Library will schedule maintenance checks for all tools every six months. Tools will be inspected for wear and tear, and any necessary repairs or replacements will be made. The maintenance schedule will be communicated to users through the tool cards, ensuring they are aware of when their tools will be checked. Additionally, a maintenance log will be kept in the library to record all maintenance activities and ensure that no tools are overlooked. Safety is the top priority at Harborlight Tool Library. The library will also have a designated area for storing tools that require special handling, such as flammable materials or sharp objects. Regular safety checks will be conducted in this area to ensure that it is secure and free from hazards. By implementing these measures, Harborlight Tool Library aims to provide a safe, efficient, and user-friendly environment for borrowing tools. The combination of the amber intake label, safety reviews, and regular maintenance will help ensure that tools are always in good condition and that safety protocols are followed. The volunteer handover system will also help in maintaining a smooth flow of tools and ensuring that no tools are left unattended or misused.

To illustrate the two-person test, let's consider a high-risk tool such as a power saw. The test involves two people: one to operate the saw and another to ensure that the saw is functioning correctly and that no safety hazards are present. The person operating the saw will start the saw and ensure that it is running smoothly. The second person will check that the blade is sharp and that there are no signs of wear or damage. They will also check that the saw is properly secured to the workbench and that there are no loose parts that could cause accidents. If either person notices any issues, they will stop the saw and address the problem before continuing. This two-person test ensures that the power saw is safe to use and that no accidents occur.
